rationale: The Court is most likely to uphold § 922(g)(3) as applied by adopting a narrowing construction of “is an unlawful user” to require contemporaneous, regular unlawful use close in time to possession, aligning the statute with Bruen/Rahimi’s analogical, danger-and-temporality-focused framework. Separate writings are most likely from Thomas (principal dissent) and possibly Barrett/Kavanaugh/Alito to emphasize the limiting construction and evidentiary rigor, with Gorsuch potentially dissenting separately on lenity/vagueness and anti-rewriting grounds.
